title: Binary Tree Level Order Traversal II
summary: For a given binary tree, provide the nodes' values in a bottom-up level order traversal, moving from the lowest level to the root level, and from left to right within each level.
statement: For a given binary tree, provide the nodes' values in a bottom-up level order traversal, moving from the lowest level to the root level, and from left to right within each level.
constraints: Return levels from deepest to shallowest while keeping values left-to-right inside each level. An empty tree returns [].

hints: Bottom-up depth order is not the same as visiting every leaf first.
Build ordinary left-to-right breadth-first levels, then reverse the outer list.
Pop one queue-width group at a time, append its values, enqueue children, and return levels[::-1].
Do not reverse the values inside a row: the left-to-right requirement is unchanged.
editorial: Group nodes by depth with a queue, retaining left-to-right order. Reversing only the completed list of rows changes depth order without changing within-level order. Nodes that are leaves at different depths do not belong in the same group. The oracle independently sorts position paths by depth and horizontal position.
